subject: Marginal log-likelihoods when there are multiple likelihoods

messages.author: 490a7efb4abf90e1
messages.subject: Marginal log-likelihoods when there are multiple likelihoods
parts:
Dear all,

In model estimated with INLA with more than one likelihood (say, using multiple stacks, e.g., 'gaussian' and 'poisson'), we are given just one posterior marginal log-likelihood number in the output. Would it be possible to disentangle this with respect to the different types of responses in the stack corresponding to the different types of likelihood?

I hope this question makes sense.

Thanks,
Jon

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Marginal log-likelihoods when there are multiple likelihoods
parts:
no, that would not be possible unless the joint posterior is a product
of independent posteriors (one for each likelihood family)
